title: Evaluation of an LLM to Generate Fusion 360 API Scripts for CAD Modeling of Industrial Robot Components and System Automation Elements
items.abstract: <jats:p>Currently, several LLMs (Large Language Models) assist users with specific tasks, such as summarizing texts or solving physics problems, to name a few. On the other hand, using scripts allows users to automate tasks and save time in their creation. This article evaluates an LLM for generating scripts for the Application Programming Interface (API) of the Fusion 360 CAD software application, to determine its capabilities for developing 3D modeling components used in the simulation of industrial robots or the automation of manufacturing systems. Among the results, it was found that the generated scripts enable modeling of industrial robots and automation elements using simple geometries that the user can later customize for a specific application. Furthermore, it is recommended that users be familiar with Fusion 360 in case they need to modify or assemble the components created by scripting. At the end, a Prompt Engineering Guide for Fusion 360 scripts focused on generating components for industrial robots is shared.</jats:p>

title: LLM Hallucinations as Ghost Theories via Formal-system Imitation
items.abstract:
<jats:p><div>
 &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Language-model hallucinations are usually judged one statement at a time. We argue that this pointwise view misses a structural mechanism. When an autoregressive model is trained on strings drawn from a formal system, it induces a stochastic inference graph; across bootstrap replicas this graph crystallises into an ensemble of weak formal systems. Some stable structures are genuine theorem-like regions anchored to the trusted axioms. Others are ghost theories: stable, internally coherent components generated by implicit ghost axioms but lacking a robust path back to the seed.&nbsp;
</div>
<div>
 &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;The framework uses four ensemble observables: stability, axiom anchoring, logical damage, and bridge risk. Together they decompose the induced theory into an anchored core, true unanchored extensions, false floating ghost theories, and high-damage failures. We prove a soundness-based truth-uniformity result for connected components of the robust graph and explain ghost formation as a consequence of next-token training, which enforces local coherence without enforcing global genealogical closure. This also gives a topological account of paraconsistency: incompatible contents need not collapse the induced theory when they remain quarantined in disconnected components.&nbsp;
</div>
<div>
 &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;Empirically, we study MIU and a bounded Robinson-Q-inspired arithmetic with equality and disequality. In MIU, anchoring reaches precision 0.976 against 0.640 for stability filtering at comparable recall. In the arithmetic setting, anchoring reaches precision 1.000 at the headline configuration, removing 33 stable false statements admitted by stability alone. The phenomenon transfers to a small Transformer trained from scratch; its largest false ghost cluster grows from 16 in the trigram setting to 38. Across 250 bootstraps spanning five independent seedbases every floating cluster is truth-uniform without exception, and approximately fifteen per cent of floating-cluster statements appear in floating clusters of every seedbase, identifying them as invariant biases of the model class on this formal system. Axiom-touch experiments further show that true-content touches yield new sound theorems, whereas false-content touches amplify falsity and sometimes break soundness without explicit contradiction. The resulting picture treats systematic hallucination not as isolated error, but as stable local inference structure without trusted genealogy.
</div></jats:p>

title: From Untrusted Documents to Trusted Industrial Transactions: Integrity-Aware InformationIntegration for LLM-Enabled Freight Logistics
items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial logistics increasingly links emails, portable-document text, and Electronic DataInterchange (EDI) messages to transportation management systems through large languagemodel (LLM)-based extraction. Yet structural interoperability does not ensure semantic integrity:syntactically valid transactions may contain values that conflict with master data, prior state, orauthenticated counterpart information and may be persisted before detection. This study introducesIntegrity-Aware Document-to-Transaction Integration (IADTI), an architecture separatingsemantic transformation, field-level evidence reconciliation, parameter-aware authorization, andtransactional commit. FreightSkillBench evaluates IADTI using 60 falsified freight-documentcases and 60 matched benign or authorized-change cases across four document representations,five high-risk field families, and five model configurations, yielding 600 primary extractionsplus 150 repeated observations. Among case-relevant fields, 280/300 benign extractions wereintegrity-valid, while 237/300 falsified inputs produced an incorrect or omitted target field.Under direct integration, 236/237 manifested errors became persistent mock-TMS state. Schemagating still committed 91.1% of manifested errors and falsely blocked 3.6% of valid benigninputs. Complete-reference reconciliation prevented all manifested incorrect commits whilepreserving 96.4% of valid benign work, but missing references detected none and adversaryalignedreferences missed 236/237. Endpoint restrictions obstructed 62.1% of valid benign tasksyet left 99.6% of manifested errors committed because an earlier permitted action stored the fullpayload. Universal approval prevented incorrect commit but escalated every valid benign input.The findings establish semantic commit integrity as a distinct industrial information-integrationrequirement and support trustworthy reference data, evidence-aware parameter authorization,validation before persistence, and selective escalation.</jats:p>

title: Selective Risk Control for LLM Decision Agents under Uncertainty

affiliation.name: Lycée Lyautey

items.abstract: Background: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as components of intelligent decision-support systems, yet many evaluations still emphasize answer accuracy or task completion without isolating when an agent should decline to act.Objectives:We study selective risk control for LLM decision agents under uncertainty, asking whether binding adversarial critique improves decision behavior or primarily changes when the system abstains. Methods: We evaluate a controlled benchmark for sparse and contradictory evidence screening with 1,200 evidence bundles, 8,100 evidence snippets, and 18,000 saved local LLM decisions across five agent architectures and three seeds. The analysis includes uncertainty strata, proxy regret, risk capture, matched-coverage controls, thresholded monolithic baselines, abstention-penalty sweeps, external checks, and a 900-call stratified rerun. Results: Binding critique behaves as a conservative risk gate. It catches substantially more proxy high-risk cases than a monolithic decision baseline and improves utility when abstention is inexpensive, but its advantage disappears under moderate abstention penalties and it does not consistently improve active decision quality at matched coverage. Thresholded monolithic controls further show that the mechanism is not a better confidence-ranking selective classifier. Conclusions: The contribution is not a claim of general decision superiority. It is an evaluation framework and design lesson for uncertainty-aware AI systems: abstention-mediated gains must be separated from genuine improvements in active decisions, and critique mechanisms should be evaluated as tunable deferral layers rather than as unconditional replacements for simpler policies.

title: Sparse Autoencoders as an Interpretable Interface for LLM Development and Control

affiliation.name: Slovak Academic Information Agency, Bratislava

items.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing capability and opacity of large language models (LLMs) necessitate robust tools for understanding and steering their internal computations. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have recently emerged as a promising bridge between the high-dimensional, distributed representations of neural networks and human-interpretable concepts. This paper explores the hypothesis that SAEs can serve as a fundamental interpretable interface for both the development and operational control of LLMs. We first demonstrate that SAEs, when trained on intermediate layer activations, reliably disentangle polysemantic neurons into sparse, mono-semantic features that correlate with specific linguistic, factual, or contextual patterns. We then show that this sparse decomposition enables novel diagnostics: by monitoring feature activations, developers can identify circuit malfunctions, bias amplification, and knowledge gaps during model training and fine-tuning. Crucially, we extend this interface to active control, introducing steering vectors derived from SAE features that allow for targeted modulation of model behavior—such as adjusting sentiment, reducing hallucination, or enforcing safety constraints—without degrading general performance or requiring retraining. Through extensive experiments on open-source LLMs, we validate that SAE-based interventions are both causally effective and more granular than traditional prompting or classifier-free guidance. Our findings position SAEs not merely as a post-hoc explanation method, but as a core component of a new paradigm for transparent LLM engineering, enabling safer deployment and more precise alignment with human values.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Guardrails: Dual Failure Modes in LLM Safety as Inverse Control-System Errors
container-title: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
items.abstract:
<jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate sensitive
domains—mental health, identity, and meaning-making—
making their failure modes consequential beyond the technical.
While safety interventions have reduced documented
harms from sycophantic AI, they have produced a new failure
class. We introduce a dual failure-mode framework modeled
as inverse control-system errors. Mode 1 (sycophantic validation)
arises from underdamped positive feedback: models
overvalidate user beliefs and amplify distress. Mode 2 (rigid
pathologization) arises from overdamped negative feedback:
safety-hardened models misclassify valid cultural, spiritual, or
identity frameworks as pathology and respond with authoritative
dismissal. Both modes share a root cause—misplaced
epistemic authority—and both produce harm through loss of
grounding. Drawing on documented cases, regulatory filings,
and professional commentary, we argue—and find evidence
consistent with the claim—that safety hardening can invert
instability rather than resolve it when epistemic stance is not
dynamically regulated. We draw a structural analogy to embodied
and situated approaches: conversational safety systems
may be incomplete when they lack epistemic and cultural
substrates for stable human-compatible interaction.</jats:p>

Evaluating Hybrid Guardrail Architectures for Prompt Injection Defense in Large Language Models
items.abstract: <jats:p>Prompt injection attacks exploit the instruction-following behavior of large language models (LLMs) by embedding adversarial directives within user-provided text. Production systems frequently deploy layered guardrail mechanisms, combining heuristic filters and model-based classifiers, to mitigate such attacks. However, rigorous empirical evaluations of these architectures under structured adversarial variation remain limited, and most deployed systems lack publicly reported performance metrics. We present a systematic evaluation of three guardrail configurations: (1) a baseline with no guardrails, (2) regex-based heuristic filtering, and (3) a hybrid architecture combining regex filtering with an LLM-based safety classifier. We construct a two-tier benchmark of 625 prompts: 400 standard-difficulty prompts (200 attacks across 8 categories, 200 benign across 11 categories) and 225 hard-difficulty prompts (175 adversarially crafted attacks across 10 categories, 50 benign across 10 categories). We measure attack block rate, miss rate, benign false-positive rate, precision, recall, and F 1-score under a single-turn threat model. On standard attacks, the hybrid configuration achieves perfect recall (100.0% block rate, 0.0% miss rate) with 5.0% benign FPR and F 1 = 0.976, while regex-only filtering blocks 75.0% of attacks with 2.5% FPR. On adversarially crafted hard attacks, the hybrid maintains near-perfect performance: 98.9% block rate with 0.0% benign FPR and F 1 = 0.994, while regex-only filtering degrades to 24.6% block rate (F 1 = 0.408). The hybrid's only failures on the hard tier occur in the benign-wrapper injection category (2 misses of 35 attempts). We identify two principal findings: (1) the hybrid classifier generalizes robustly to adversarial attack variations, losing only 1.1 percentage points in recall from standard to hard; and (2) false positives concentrate exclusively in security-adjacent benign categories on the standard tier (security research: 87.5% FPR; critique: 37.5%), while the hard tier's generalpurpose benign prompts produce zero false positives. Our results demonstrate that hybrid architectures can achieve robust adversarial performance, though the semantic overlap between legitimate security discourse and attack signatures remains a persistent challenge for input-level classification.</jats:p>

title: Optimizing Multi‑Agent LLM Collaboration via Communication‑Flow Control​
items.abstract: <jats:p>Multi-agent systems based on Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating complex engineering tasks, including code generation for Finite Element Analysis (FEA). However, despite models demonstrating the capability to produce correct solutions, task success rates remain low. This study investigates the mechanisms limiting the effectiveness of multi-agent LLM collaboration through two complementary perspectives: agent role composition and communication flow dynamics. We evaluate seven agent combinations across four increasingly complex FEA tasks through 1,120 controlled experimental trials using the AutoGen framework with GPT-3.5-Turbo.  From the agent-role perspective, we find that neither adding more reviewers nor varying team composition yields consistent performance gains; instead, agents designed to provide critical evaluation fail to do so in practice. From a communication-flow perspective, we identify early agreements (i.e., approval messages such as ‘looks good’ or ‘execution succeeded’ that may falsely indicate task completion) as a dominant failure mechanism that prematurely halts iterative code refinement, leaving the model’s coding capability systematically underutilized. Based on these findings, we suggest an approach to optimize communication flow: removing misleading agreements while preserving necessary guidance. This approach significantly improves task success rates (Task 2: 10.7% to 77.5%; Tasks 3-4: 0.7% to 45.0%) without requiring additional training or external information. These results establish that communication dynamics, rather than agent quantity or role diversity, are the primary determinant of multi-agent collaboration effectiveness in engineering code generation.</jats:p>

title: A quantitative risk assessment method for industrial control system safety and security
items.abstract: <jats:p>With the deep integration of industrialisation and informatisation, risks within the cyber domain of industrial control systems can propagate to the physical domain. It faces dual risks in both the cyber domain and the physical domain. However, the current studies tends to focus on a single security risk assessment or safety risk assessment, thereby failing to consider risk propagation of cross domain. To fill the gap, a quantitative risk assessment method for industrial control system safety and security. Firstly, we employs Petri Nets to model security risk propagation paths, utilises fault trees to model safety risk propagation paths, and combines fault trees with Petri Nets to model safety security risk propagation paths. Then, conduct a quantitative likelihood analysis of a risk propagation path. We utilises expert elicitation to evaluate likelihood of safety risk propagation paths, combining intrusion strength, importance of devices, and exploiting vulnerability to evaluate likelihood of security risk propagation paths. Finally, we benchmark our proposed method on a open-source testing environment, GRFICS, with extensive experiments. the results substantiate the viability and effectiveness of our model.</jats:p>

title: A Segmented Adaptive PID Temperature Control Method Suitable for Industrial Gluing System
items.abstract: <jats:p>There are many parts in industrial gluing systems, and the temperature characteristics of these parts vary greatly. In response to this situation, a segmented adaptive PID temperature control method is proposed in this paper. This method combines a segmented temperature control algorithm with a variable control coefficient temperature control algorithm based on output power, which not only ensures that the system has a small overshoot but also ensures that the system has faster convergence speed and better robustness. At the same time, it greatly improves the scope of application and control accuracy of the temperature controller. The experimental results show that, under the same experimental conditions, compared with the traditional PID method, the overshoot of the proposed method is reduced by 2 to 4 degrees Celsius, the convergence speed is increased by about 30%, and the temperature fluctuation amplitude after being disturbed is reduced by about 0.2 degrees Celsius.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of LLM-Based AI Chatbots on Industrial Structure: A Marcusean Perspective
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores the impact of large language model (LLM)-based AI chatbots, particularly focusing on OpenAI's ChatGPT, on the structure of industry from a Marcusean perspective. The emergence of ChatGPT has led to rapid changes across various industries, raising important questions about the relationship between individuals, society, and the media. The study aims to analyze the interaction between one-dimensional human beings and media, considering ChatGPT as a form of media itself. It examines the positive changes brought about by AI chatbot technologies, such as enhanced data rights, diversity in expressing opinions, and strengthened education and collaboration. On the other hand, this study also addresses the negative aspects, including potential job displacement, privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, and the suppression of creativity. Through a critical analysis from a Marcusean perspective, this study sheds light on the implications of AI technologies like ChatGPT on individual freedom, power structures, and the formation of one-dimensional individuals within the industrial structure. It concludes by emphasizing the need for transparent systems, open collaboration, and the safeguarding of individual rights and freedoms in the context of AI advancements. By doing so, this study seeks to stimulate further societal engagement and a reevaluation of the Marcusean perspective in the current era.</jats:p>

Guardrail impact simulation for remote guided vehicles (RGV's) used in nuclear generating stations
items.abstract:
<jats:p>During nuclear station refurbishment, transportation of tools, equipment, and irradiated reactor components is achieved using remote guided vehicles (RGV’s) in order to keep worker radiation doses as low as reasonably achievable.
A removable guardrail system capable of withstanding RGV impact was developed to eliminate the risk of accidents taking place in the reactor vault. The guardrails are mounted to platform edges using two bolts and two shear pins. In anticipation of frequent removal of reinstallation of guardrails by workers, this study proposes that guardrails be installed without bolting, relying solely on the guardrails’ shear pins to provide the required restraint.
A parametric impact simulation was carried out in order to evaluate the perform of the guardrails when installed without bolting. The analysis work was carried out using LS-DYNA, an advanced simulation software package capable of simulating real world problems using explicit time integration.</jats:p>

title: IOBA: A Compiled Intent-Oriented Backend Guardrail Architecture with Formal Semantics and Simulation-Based Evaluation
items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents IOBA (Intent-Oriented Backend Architecture), a compiled domain-specific language (DSL) framework for structured backend guardrail enforcement. IOBA models business workflows as formally defined intent functions composed of ordered constraint-enforced steps. The DSL is compiled into deterministic validation logic integrated with runtime telemetry. We analyze empirical telemetry data from 100 simulated requests through a three-step checkout flow (validate cart → authorize payment → create order) with randomized contexts and probabilistic failure injection. Results demonstrate bounded enforcement overhead (mean flow latency 281.9 ms), short-circuit efficiency (14.3% time savings on failed flows), and structured step-level observability. The evaluation validates IOBA's core mechanisms while identifying areas for production hardening, positioning IOBA as a foundation for intent-aware backend governance.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Every day on roads many scenarios of accidents may occur. One of the measures to minimize their consequences is road safety barriers. Finite Element analyses are being increasingly used to support the physical testing of these devices. The paper addresses the issue of a secondary impact into the previously damaged w-beam guardrail system. This situation belongs to one of the most dangerous which can happen on roads and may cause serious hazards, especially if the vehicle goes through the barrier. To evaluate the crashworthiness of the road barrier, the computational model of the crash test was developed and validated against the full-scale crash test. Then two simulations of TB32 crash tests were conducted on both damaged and undamaged road barriers to assess the influence of damage on the effectiveness of the safety system during vehicular impact. <p>Yellow Guardrail Pattern Geometry Affects Drivers' Visual Attention and Vehicle Control at High-Risk Road Approaches: A Multimodal Driving-Simulator Study&nbsp;</p>
items.abstract: <jats:p>At-grade intersections and long downgrades are road environments prone to traffic crashes. Effective roadside warning design is therefore important for supporting timely hazard detection and appropriate vehicle control in these settings. Roadside color treatments can change when drivers notice a hazard and how they control the vehicle, but the role of pattern geometry remains unclear. Forty-two licensed drivers completed a 2×4 within-subject driving-simulator experiment that combined an at-grade intersection and a long downgrade with untreated, horizontal-intermittent, longitudinal-striped, and full-yellow guardrails. Target detection and first-fixation distance were derived from the full target-visible approach; visual-sampling, physiological, and vehicle outcomes were analyzed in the 50–250 m approach window using trial-level participant-fixed-effects models. Averaged across the three yellow layouts, warning-area fixation increased by 1.41 s and mean speed decreased by 11.41 km/h relative to control. Full coverage was first fixated 40.34 m farther upstream than the patterned mean and produced the lowest speed, together with an acceleration tail that was 0.66 m/s² more negative. Horizontal intermittency produced the longest warning-area fixation, the fewest gaze transitions, and the lowest steering demand. The findings separate early acquisition, sustained visual sampling, speed reduction, braking intensity, and steering demand as design criteria. Full coverage favored early acquisition and stronger slowing, whereas horizontal intermittency favored sustained attention and lower steering demand.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper proposes an intelligent industrial setpoint tracking control approach using an output recurrent elliptic fuzzy broad learning system (Elliptic ORFBLS). This approach integrates the strengths of intelligent control, which effectively manages complex nonlinear systems with an adaptive identification mechanism that efficiently handles uncertain parameters in unknown systems. The adaptive mechanism notably enhances transient state responses, leading to faster rise times and reduced overshoot, while ensuring stable and precise setpoint tracking in the steady state. Three theorems are presented to guarantee system convergence, stability, and applicability. Additionally, a comprehensive study on time complexity and memory consumption is included to assist practitioners in controller selection. Through comparative simulations and experimental validations, this control strategy is shown to offer a robust and effective solution for challenging nonlinear systems.</jats:p>

title: Guardrail Shadow Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Systems (Safety Layers Distorting RAG Outputs)
items.abstract: <jats:p>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are designed to anchor large language models in verified evidence. In controlled settings, retrieval improves factual accuracy and reduces hallucination risk. In production environments, however, an under-examined failure mode is emerging. Stacked safety layers surrounding the generation stage can subtly distort how retrieved evidence is expressed, resulting in answers that remain compliant but become diluted, hedged, or operationally weakened. This paper defines this phenomenon as the Guardrail Shadow Effect (GSE). The proposed framework introduces the Shadow Impact Score (SIS) to quantify when high-quality retrieved context fails to translate into proportionate answer strength. Rather than auditing safety filters or retrieval quality in isolation, the method models cross-layer interaction between retrieval confidence, policy pressure, and generation behaviour. The architecture is model-agnostic and suitable for enterprise knowledge copilots, regulated-domain assistants, and internal RAG deployments. Evaluation across controlled simulations shows that guardrail pressure can materially reduce evidence utilization even when retrieval precision remains stable. The findings expose a structural blind spot in current RAG observability: grounding can succeed while usefulness quietly degrades. Detecting and managing guardrail shadow dynamics will be essential for organizations that want RAG systems to remain both safe and decisively useful.</jats:p>

title: A Hybrid Agency Framework: Modeling Human-LLM Interaction as a Cybernetic System
items.abstract: <jats:p>Generative large-language models (LLMs) are evolving from passive tools into adaptive cognitive partners. This paper proposes the Hybrid Agency Framework (HAF), a conceptual model that treats the human-LLM dyad as a single, integrated cybernetic system. Drawing from the traditions of joint cognitive systems and control theory, HAF moves beyond the prevalent "blind prompting" paradigm, where users operate with limited insight into the model's state and bear full liability for its outputs. We formalize the collaborative process as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), providing a principled, control-theoretic foundation for managing interaction. The framework's central contribution is a model of bidirectional alignment, where both the human's expressed preferences and the LLM's policy co-adapt in real-time within a shared cognitive workspace. This contrasts sharply with current one-way alignment methods (e.g., RLHF) that treat user preferences as static targets for model training. Furthermore, HAF integrates a multi-stakeholder governance matrix explicitly mapped to emerging regulatory standards (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001) to distribute accountability. This paper presents the complete conceptual design, including its theoretical underpinnings, a formal POMDP specification, a multifactor skill-retention protocol to mitigate user de-skilling, and a detailed plan for future empirical validation. By framing human-LLM interaction as a controllable cybernetic system, HAF offers a rigorous roadmap toward safer, more transparent, and genuinely collaborative hybrid intelligence.</jats:p>

title: AI as a Constituted System: Accountability Lessons from an LLM Experiment
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores the integration of a pre-trained Large Language Model (LLM) with an organisation's Knowledge Management System (KMS) via a chat interface, focusing on the practicalities of establishing and maintaining AI infrastructure for data storage and access, and the considerations to ensure responsible governance. The study adopts the concept of ‘AI as a constituted system’ to emphasise that the social, technical, and institutional factors that contribute to AI’s governance and accountability. Through an ethnographic approach, the paper details the iterative processes of negotiation, decision-making, and reflection among stakeholders as they develop, implement, and manage the AI system. The study reveals that LLMs can be effectively governed and held accountable to the interests of stakeholders within specific contexts, when facilitated by clear institutional boundaries that foster innovation, while navigating risks related to data privacy and AI misbehaviours. This is attributed to distinct policy creation processes guiding the AI's operation, clear lines of responsibility, and localised feedback loops that ensured clear accountability for actions taken. This research offers a foundational perspective to better understand accountability and governance of algorithms within organisational contexts. It also suggests a future where AI is not universally scaled but consists of localised, customised LLMs that are tailored to stakeholder interests.</jats:p>

Lightweight Adaptive YOLOv11 for Industrial Defect Perception and Closed-Loop Sorting Cybernetic Control System
items.abstract: Industrial surface defect inspection and automatic sorting control constitute critical feedback links in intelligent manufacturing cybernetic systems. Conventional detection methods suffer from bulky model parameters, low inference speed, and weak anti-interference capability under uneven illumination, tiny defect targets and surface occlusion, failing to satisfy the millisecond-level closed-loop feedback constraints of industrial production control. Targeting the disconnection between machine learning visual detection and industrial automatic control in existing YOLO-based research, this paper proposes a lightweight adaptive YOLOv11 detector and constructs a complete machine-learning-perception-driven closed-loop sorting cybernetic control system. First, a Lightweight Coordinate Adaptive Attention (LCAA) module is embedded into the YOLOv11 C2f backbone to boost feature extraction for tiny blurred defects while compressing redundant parameters. Second, an adaptive multi-scale feature fusion mechanism is designed for the neck network to dynamically adjust fusion weights according to target scale variation, mitigating multi-scale defect missing detection. Finally, the optimized lightweight model is deployed on edge embedded hardware, and real-time detection outputs act as state feedback signals for the sorting controller to establish a full perception-decision-execution negative feedback control loop. Experiments on the public NEU steel defect dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 97.2% mAP@0.5, with parameters reduced by 28.6% and inference speed increased by 32.1% compared with vanilla YOLOv11. Physical edge sorting platform tests verify the closed-loop system maintains an overall end-to-end delay below 50 ms, sorting success rate of 98.5% and steady-state error less than 2%. This work delivers an integrated machine learning perception-cybernetic control solution for industrial intelligent manufacturing, matching the interdisciplinary positioning of machine learning and cybernetics.

title: Multi-Disease AI Diagnosis System Using Minimal Code and LLM-Powered Explanations
items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a novel approach to multi-disease diagnosis using a lightweight neural network architecture combined with large language model (LLM) powered explanations. We demonstrate how modern AI assistants can enable rapid development of functional healthcare AI systems with minimal code implementation. Our system achieves 72% accuracy on synthetic multi-disease classification tasks (Diabetes, Parkinson's Disease, and Healthy classifications) while providing human-readable explanations for each diagnosis through an integrated LLM reasoning module. The complete system, implemented in under 500 lines of code, demonstrates end-to-end functionality from data generation to model deployment, showcasing the potential for democratizing AI healthcare development. Key contributions include: (1) a streamlined architecture combining neural networks with LLM explanations, (2) automatic symbolic rule extraction for high-confidence predictions, (3) a deployable model export system, and (4) transparent documentation of AI-assisted development methodologies.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>Distributed bioenergy renewable power networks face an unresolved equity challenge: AI‐governed dispatch optimisers maximise aggregate throughput while systematically under‐serving peripheral nodes. This paper presents ethical guardrail bandit pruning, a fairness‐constrained reinforcement learning system enforcing equity and energy sustainability via a two‐timescale primal‐dual guardrail, coupling a bandit‐gradient importance estimator, an ethical guardrail buffer, cost‐weighted pruning and guardrail‐filtered federated averaging over a constrained Markov decision process. Convergence was checked against logged gradient norms and found shallower than theory predicts. A 5000‐round extended‐horizon run (50,000 local steps) remained within the safety threshold in  of rounds; multi‐seed extended‐horizon verification is future work. Results operationalise SDG 7, 10, 12 and 13 as verifiable engineering guardrails.</jats:p>

title: The Formalization Threshold and Selection Effect: A Complexity Grading Criterion and Human–LLM Framework from Eight Industrial Cases
items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial AI methods for detection, recognition, and prediction share an entry condition that is rarely stated: the problem must first be formalized into defined objects, variables, and labels. For high-value, cross-domain, system-level non-standard problems, formalization is itself the most expensive step, with costs arising at the physical, cognitive, and organizational levels. The consequence is a selection effect. Problems that can be formalized get solved and leave the pool; the problems that accumulate on the shop floor are systematically those hardest to formalize. Large language models do not require prior formalization. What they change is the cost structure of problem definition, not the physical difficulty of the problem. The study then proposes an L1–L4 grading with a six-feature complexity criterion and a five-stage human–LLM collaborative framework. Validation draws on eight real industrial cases spanning steel rolling, water treatment, continuous-casting electrics, materials development, industrial software, and industrial networks. In the two in-depth cases the complexity score fell from 15 to 7 and 8, with the drop concentrated in the structural items that capture definition difficulty; of three independent double ratings, two agreed at band level and the third fell one band adjacent. A contrasting pair of third-party collaborations marks where the mechanism stops: executed under the framework, a months-long intermittent fault was localized within half a day; used as naive question-answering, the collaboration did not converge, because a key temporal cue never entered the problem representation. On this evidence the binding constraint is representation completeness rather than model capability.</jats:p>

title: Guardian Angel: A Last-Mile Virtue-Ethics Guardrail for Decentralized Agentic AI Safety
items.abstract: <jats:p>Agentic AI systems introduce novel safety challenges that upstream alignment layers cannot fully address. Prompt injection, emotional manipulation, and infrastructure-disabling actions can bypass model-level safeguards, leading to unauthorized tool executions with real-world consequences. We present Guardian Angel, a deployable plugin for open agent frameworks (e.g., OpenClaw/ClawHub) that enforces moral oversight at the last mile-immediately before tool calls-via a privileged before_tool_call hook. Grounded in Thomistic virtue ethics and centered on caritas (the willing of the principal's genuine good), the system maintains a continuous virtuous disposition while applying triggered three-gate evaluation: provenance classification, intrinsic-evil hard stops, and virtue-based scoring using a Clarity × Stakes matrix. Questionable actions escalate to human approval via cryptographically bound, time-limited nonces. The design exploits a key structural property of agentic systems-the sparsity of tool calls relative to internal reasoning-to integrate fast System 1 filtering with deliberate System 2 moral reasoning, thereby decentralizing safety to end-users without prohibitive latency. We discuss the philosophical prerequisites for such systems, detail the architecture and implementation, present qualitative evaluation results from red-team testing, and outline directions for formal benchmarking. Guardian Angel is MIT-0 licensed and available at https://clawhub.ai/leo3linbeck/guardian-angel.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Industrial robot is a and multi‐output complex system with strong coupling and high nonlinearity. The motion control accuracy of the system is affected by many factors. To solve the difficulty in establishing the input and output characteristics of robot dynamics modeling, the robot motion model is established through the Lagrangian energy function. At the same time, the nonlinear relationship between angular velocity, angular acceleration, and robot torque is accurately expressed through improved cascaded neural network. In addition, the optimal time planning of the robot's trajectory in joint space is studied using multinomial interpolation method and the particle swarm optimization (PSO). In the simulation experiment, the effect of the proposed dynamic model fitting was outstanding. Under the mixed multinomial difference calculation planning, the angular position trajectories of the three joints changed very smoothly. In the data set application test, the average error of the PSO algorithm was 0.4061 mm and the average task time was 9.101 s, which were lower than other planning algorithms. Experiments showed that the Lagrangian dynamic model analysis based on genetic algorithm cascaded neural network and PSO trajectory scheduling method under mixed multinomial difference had better trajectory planning performance in handling tasks.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>With the development of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology, multimachine collaborative operations have become the core model for increasing mission effectiveness. However, large-scale UAV clusters face challenges such as dynamic security threats, heterogeneous data fusion difficulties, and resource-constrained decision-making delays. Traditional single-machine intelligent architectures have limitations when addressing new threats, such as insufficient real-time response capabilities. To address these issues, this paper presnts an LLM-layered collaborative security architecture (LLM-LCSA) for multimachine collaborative security. This architecture optimizes the spatiotemporal fusion efficiency of multisource asynchronous data through cloud–edge–end collaborative deployment, combining an end lightweight LLM, an edge medium LLM, and a cloud-based foundation LLM. Additionally, a Mixture of Experts (MoEs) intelligent algorithm that dynamically activates the most relevant expert models by leveraging a threat–expert association matrix is introduced, thereby increasing the accuracy of complex threat identification and dynamic adaptability. Moreover, a resource-aware multi-objective optimization model is constructed to generate optimal decisions under resource constraints. Simulation results indicate that compared with traditional methods, LLM-LCSA achieves an average 7.92% improvement in the threat detection accuracy, reduces the system’s total response time by 44.52%, and enables resource scheduling during off-peak periods. This architecture provides an efficient, intelligent, and scalable solution for secure collaboration among UAV swarms. Future research should further explore its application potential in 6G network integration and large-scale swarm environments.</jats:p>

title: A  Priority-ordered Decision Model for Educational LLM Agents
Модель ухвалення рішень з пріоритетизацією сигналів для освітніх LLM-агентів
items.abstract: <jats:p>This work is devoted to the design of a decision-support architecture for artificial intelligence agents used in higher-education. The paper proposes a priority-ordered decision model that ranks three evaluation signals – divergence between self-assessment and teacher assessment, performance trend, and peer comparison – before any call to a language model, so that the same input data always yields the same intervention priority. The model is based on a deterministic progress-weighting service defined by equations (1) – (9), with a course-configurable divergence threshold (τ = 0.15 in the reference configuration) and four weight coefficients that sum to 1. The paper develops a reference implementation with a typed evidence schema, a FastAPI backend, and a tool-augmented LLM agent restricted to four read-only tools. A worked example shows that a flagged divergence (d = 0.25 > τ) overrides an improving trend (L: 0.58 → 0.64 → 0.67), correctly prioritizing a calibration alert over a routine update. The results can be used to design auditable, LLM-based recommendation systems for education and other domains where several evidence signals must be reconciled before a generative model is invoked.</jats:p>

title: A MULTI-VECTOR GUARDRAIL FRAMEWORK FOR SECURE KNOWLEDGE ENGINEERING IN AUTONOMOUS INTELLIGENT SYSTEM
items.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter introduces a modular architectural framework for securing the lifecycle of autonomous intelligent systems. As AI transitions from traditional data processing to advanced Knowledge Engineering, the necessity for robust safety mechanisms becomes critical. This article describes how to integrate multi-vector guardrails—specifically focusing on backend validation, real-time adversarial purification, and deterministic logic—into the control flow of autonomous agents. The speedy development of agentic AI in recent years has made it a popular direction for research in smart applications, but it also introduces risks such as data poisoning and model hallucinations. This study presents an efficient approach to mitigating these risks by implementing a layered security architecture. The research evaluates the effectiveness of these safety protocols without compromising computational performance, providing a blueprint for inherently secure intelligent systems.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Objetivo: Diseñar e implementar un asistente conversacional multimodal embebido en hardware de borde para entornos industriales, resolviendo la ausencia de interfaces locales especializadas en la atención comercial y técnica. Metodología: Mediante investigación aplicada, se desarrolló una arquitectura modular integrada en una tarjeta NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier. El sistema sincroniza tres formas de interacción mediante procesamiento multihilo: visión artificial con MediaPipe para activación gestual; procesamiento bidireccional de voz con Whisper para transcripción (STT) y motores híbridos para síntesis (TTS); e inferencia local mediante Ollama. Para optimizar el rendimiento y asegurar baja latencia sin dependencia de la nube, se aplicó procesamiento selectivo por lotes, fragmentación de texto (chunking) en el TTS y optimización en GPU CUDA. La validación experimental evaluó la consistencia semántica y el consumo de hardware desplegando el modelo ligero Qwen2.5 (500 millones de parámetros) alimentado con una base de conocimiento corporativa. Resultados: Las pruebas demostraron estabilidad operativa e interacciones libres de alucinaciones. El sistema registró una latencia promedio de 17.24 ms por token, rendimiento de 58.53 tokens por segundo, y un consumo eficiente de recursos del 22.69% en memoria y 10.77% en CPU. Discusiones: La fluidez y longitud de las respuestas continuas se encuentran supeditadas a la tasa de compresión de tokens del modelo de lenguaje y a la latencia inherente del motor de traducción de voz. Conclusiones: El desarrollo valida la viabilidad de ejecutar modelos de lenguaje pequeños en la periferia industrial. Su diseño modular y la flexibilidad para reconfigurar roles mediante archivos de texto garantizan su escalabilidad en la Industria 5.0.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The development of industrial robotics technology has led to a large number of applications in assembly tasks in production practice, but due to factors such as the complexity of the assembly process, the robot's own positioning accuracy and the limitations of vision technology, there are still great challenges in the control of high-precision assembly of robots. In this paper, a high-precision assembly industrial robot automatic control and servo control system combined with flexible assembly technology is proposed. In this system, an actuation system and a mechanics perception system are designed. The actuation system is based on 6PUS-UPU parallel robots, and the motion control of the assembly robot is realized by kinematic inverse solution. The mechanics sensing system is constructed based on a six-dimensional force sensor as a way to obtain the force/torque data during the assembly process of the industrial robot. Then the robot motion model is linearized using the variational method, and then an ideal impedance model is set for the adjustable parametric impedance control system to realize the supple control of the industrial robot with reference to the adaptive control method. It is found that the optimized automatic control and servo control system of the high-precision assembly industrial robot in this paper has higher assembly efficiency and strong fault-tolerant assembly effect. Therefore, the optimization of the automatic control and servo control system of high-precision assembly industrial robots can lay a solid foundation for improving the industrial production level.</jats:p>

title: Causal Graph Constrained LLM for Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Data Centers

items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial data-center systems contain complex component dependencies and long fault-propagation chains, making accurate root-cause localization difficult. Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising solution because of their strong ability to understand, organize, and reason over heterogeneous operational evidence. However, existing LLM-based methods mainly rely on statistical co-occurrence in pretraining corpora and may mistake correlation for causation in complex systems. In this paper, we propose CALM, a causally constrained LLM framework for fault diagnosis. The main idea is to learn the causal structure among fault units induced by system dependencies and use it to constrain the LLM reasoning process. Specifically, we train a graph neural network with independently learnable edge gates, impose sparsity directly on these gates, and validate the retained edges using post-training nonlinear Granger predictive gains. The resulting causal relationships constrain the LLM to trace root causes reliably. Experiments on a dataset collected from a power metering data center show that the proposed method achieves a root-cause localization accuracy of 82.6%, outperforming the best-performing baseline by 9.2 percentage points. The method also outputs explicit fault-propagation paths, indicating that causal-structure constraints can improve both the accuracy and interpretability of fault diagnosis.</jats:p>
